issues.description: The problem statement is internally inconsistent about the collection type for Farm.animals: the UML diagram shows animals: List<Animal> while the textual instructions in Part 3 explicitly require using a Set implemented as a HashSet (to ensure uniqueness). The provided solution implements animals as a List (ArrayList), and the template does not initialize or declare the collection. This mismatch affects the expected behavior (uniqueness of animals) and the required types for the getter/setter/constructor, which may confuse students and lead to implementations that do not satisfy the textual requirement or the tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the specification and code: decide whether Farm.animals should be a List or a Set. If uniqueness is required (as the text states), update the UML and all references in the problem statement to specify Set<Animal> and HashSet. Then update the template and solution to declare animals as a Set<Animal>, initialize it with new HashSet<>(), and change the getter and setter signatures accordingly (use Set<Animal>). If List behavior was intended instead, change the textual instructions to refer to a List and remove the HashSet requirement.
